benchmarking_db 1340: ERR33-C valkey oracle build, from scratch. This batch is Formatted-output callees whose result is assigned but never tested, plus the conversion, allocation and environment families: snprintf/vsnprintf/printf/sscanf/strftime assigned-shape, strtoll/strtoull/strtol/strtoul, strdup/strndup/malloc/realloc, time/localtime, getenv. 123 rows, 87 TP / 36 FP. The task's 351 in-scope run-265 findings are split across three batches (b1 104, b2 124, b3 123 = 351; 304 TP / 47 FP overall).

SCOPE. All 351 run-265 ERR33-C valkey findings are in scope under data/benchmark_repos.json's valkey predicate (scope_include src/*.c, src/*.h, src/trace/**, src/modules/lua/**; scope_exclude src/modules/*.c, src/unit/**), applied with aurora-lint's own bench.corpus.in_scope rather than a re-implementation. Nothing was dropped: the runner's --exclude already removes the out-of-scope trees, so in-scope == the full 351. No scope question was open (coordinator, 2026-09-19).

BASIS. run 265 = sqc-0.4.336-f48effe3, pulled via benchmarking_db's sqc-benchmark-query list_realworld_unlabeled (run=265, rule=ERR33-C, project=valkey): total_unlabeled 351, returned 351, truncated false, per_project run_findings 372 / labeled 21. Counting basis is distinct (project, commit, file, line, rule) keys. Verified against the CSV before appending: 0 collisions with any existing valkey row, 0 collisions with the 21 existing ERR33-C rows, 0 duplicate keys within the batch. No precision or recall claim is made here.

BAR. ADR-0001, quoted: a rule reports violations as written, and "the one real exception" -- the only thing that makes a finding FP -- is that "the finding doesn't actually match what the rule's text describes at all (wrong AST node, wrong operand, misattributed line, a check that never encodes real semantics)". So TP = the return value genuinely is not checked; FP = the analyzer misread the code and the value IS checked. Consistent with task-1271's bar. "Ignoring this call is reasonable here" (advisory flush, debug print, startup code, OOM-is-fatal, truncation-into-a-big-buffer) is a suppression/config question and never an FP ground.

A USE IS NOT A CHECK. The single most common error in adjudicating this rule, and the one that moved the most verdicts in this pass: a later expression that CONSUMES the value is not a test of its FAILURE MODE. `time_t now = time(NULL)` followed by `now - last > interval` is arithmetic, not a test for (time_t)-1. `current_epoch = strtoull(s, NULL, 10)` followed by `if (current_epoch > sentinel.current_epoch)` is business logic, not an error check. `buflen = snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, ...)` followed by `if (connWrite(conn, buf, buflen) != buflen)` validates the WRITER, not the formatter -- buflen is never compared to 0 or sizeof(buf). All three shapes are TP. Conversely `l += snprintf(...)` followed by `if (l >= bufsize) break;` IS the truncation predicate and is FP.

METHOD. Preliminary mechanical triage by shape, then every one of the 133 non-bare findings read at the pinned checkout by a reviewing agent with the bar above, and the 218 bare ones verified mechanically (named callee present on every cited line -- 0 misattributions; no (void) cast, no macro body, no return-expression context) and reasoned from the callee's documented failure mode. Second opinion applied by the submitting adjudicator on every flagged case; one verdict was overturned on review (src/hashtable.c:2488, FP -> TP: the truncation guard at line 2505 is inside `if (full)`, so on the full==0 path l is never tested, and on the full path the untested value is consumed as `bufsize - l` at 2493 where a truncating return underflows the size_t argument).

DIVERGENCE FROM THE HISTORICAL CORPUS -- READ THIS BEFORE COMPARING RATES. This batch's TP rate is higher than older ERR33-C labels in other projects for two callees, and the cause is the bar, not the code: fflush 100% TP here vs 46% historically, time 100% vs 39%. The historical FPs in those classes are reasoned as "advisory", "standard REPL practice", "failure acceptable (degraded entropy only)" -- grounds ADR-0001 explicitly rejects. task-1271's own manifest already records this as "KNOWN INCONSISTENCY, NOT TOUCHED" (~40 older ERR33-C FP rows across other projects that are TP under this bar) and leaves it to the coordinator as gavel_review territory. Nothing outside valkey was touched here. Two other divergences are NOT bar-driven and were checked at source: strdup 57% TP here vs 7% historically is genuine (valkey-benchmark parseOptions assigns 7 config.sslconfig.* fields from strdup(argv[++i]) with no NULL test anywhere), and malloc 50% vs 5% is n=4.

ANALYZER GAP WORTH FILING (not a label question). 14 of the 47 FPs are one shape: an accumulator `x += snprintf(...)` whose truncation is tested later as `x >= size` / `x + 1 > size`, which the rule does not follow (valkey hashtable.c, util.c ld2string, fuzzer_command_generator printCommand, valkey-benchmark). A second, cheaper one: strto* with a literal NULL endptr is a near-perfect TP predictor in this tree while strto* with &eptr is a near-perfect FP predictor (every config.c setter validates *eptr), so following the endptr argument would remove most of the remaining conversion-family noise. Recommended as an aurora_lint task; no rule change is proposed by this batch.

OBSERVATION, NOT ACTED ON. src/fuzzer_client.c (10 findings) and src/fuzzer_command_generator.c (2) are a fuzzing harness rather than the shipped server, but they are top-level src/*.c and therefore in scope under the declared predicate, which the coordinator confirmed closed. They are labeled. If a future scope review wants them out, that is a benchmark_repos.json change, not a relabel.
